elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without consent to an affiliate.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly states that Customer may assign the Agreement without consent to an affiliate.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without consent to a successor in a merger.
elements.evidence: The successor exception permits assignment by merger notwithstanding the consent requirement.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without consent to a successor in an acquisition.
elements.evidence: The successor exception permits assignment by acquisition notwithstanding the consent requirement.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without consent to a successor in a sale of substantially all assets.
elements.evidence: The successor exception expressly includes a sale of substantially all assets.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign this Agreement or its rights without Customer's prior consent.
elements.evidence: The mutual opening sentence requires IBM to obtain Customer's prior written consent before assigning the Agreement or any rights under it.

elements.element: Customer may not unreasonably withhold consent to a Vendor assignment.
elements.evidence: The mutual consent requirement expressly provides that consent may not be unreasonably withheld.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign this Agreement to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: The clause unconditionally states that IBM will not assign the Agreement to a competitor of Customer.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination right based on Customer's change of control.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause creates no termination right for IBM based on a Customer change of control.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement to a successor without consent.
elements.evidence: The Customer successor exception overrides the general consent requirement.

elements.element: Customer must provide Vendor written notice of a successor assignment.
elements.evidence: No written-notice obligation applies to Customer's successor assignments.

elements.element: Vendor may assign this Agreement to a successor without consent.
elements.evidence: IBM receives no successor exception and remains subject to Customer's prior written consent for all assignments.

elements.element: Vendor must provide Customer written notice of a successor assignment.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no written-notice obligation for an IBM successor assignment.

elements.element: Customer assignments other than successor assignments require Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent, even though an affiliate assignment need not be a successor assignment.

elements.element: Vendor may not unreasonably withhold consent to Customer assignments other than successor assignments.
elements.evidence: For Customer assignments subject to consent, the opening sentence provides that IBM's consent may not be unreasonably withheld.

elements.element: Vendor assignments other than successor assignments require Customer consent.
elements.evidence: The opening sentence requires Customer's prior written consent for every IBM assignment; the competitor prohibition imposes an additional restriction but does not remove the consent requirement.

elements.element: Customer may not unreasonably withhold consent to Vendor assignments other than successor assignments.
elements.evidence: The mutual consent language expressly provides that Customer's consent may not be unreasonably withheld.

result.reason: The operative language satisfies every preferred requirement: Customer receives the specified affiliate and successor carve-outs, IBM is subject to Customer consent and an absolute competitor prohibition, and no change-of-control termination right is created. The fallback is not satisfied because there is no written-notice mechanism, IBM lacks a consent-free successor right, and Customer's affiliate carve-out exceeds the fallback consent regime for non-successor assignments. The redline is substantively focused and preserves the original void-assignment and continuing-liability provisions. Minor drafting weaknesses are the appended placement of the affiliate/competitor sentence and the awkward phrase 'successor organization by ... sale of substantially all assets.'
